children: Consumer sentiment in the U.K. tumbled at the fastest pace since the Covid-19 pandemic this month as mounting cost-of-living pressures reversed the bounce in optimism seen over the summer.

Research group GfK said its consumer-confidence barometer, published Friday with the Nuremberg Institute for Market Decisions, fell 11 points to minus 24 in October--the largest fall in sentiment since the onset of the pandemic in April 2020.
The result was significantly lower than a consensus of economists polled by The Wall Street Journal, which forecast a reading of minus 14.
"The summer's buoyant mood has evaporated. The speed of this deterioration is alarming," said Neil Bellamy, consumer insights director at GfK.

Consumers in the U.K. face rising cost-of-living pressures as the war in Iran continues to push up energy prices. Data published Wednesday showed inflation rising further above the Bank of England's target in August, increasing the likelihood that the central bank will raise interest rates at its next meeting on Nov. 5.

The fall in sentiment for October was driven mainly by worsening consumer expectations for the U.K. economy in the coming year, as well as a slump in intentions to make major purchases, according to GfK.

The U.K. economy defied expectations of a slowdown in activity following the outbreak of war in the Middle East, expanding by 1.2% in the first half of the year. Still, a steep contraction in consumer confidence could dent hopes that this resilience will continue into the final quarter of 2026.
"With weakness seen across the full spectrum of income, age and gender demographic groups, these are damaging findings given the U.K. government's priority of economic growth," Bellamy said.
Write to Don Nico Forbes at don.forbes@wsj.com

title: U.K. Consumer Confidence Suffers Biggest Drop Since Pandemic
